utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom and outside -- and to those outside watching and listening to this trial. Could the Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we start the conference, I would like to ask you, Mr. Tolimir -- Mr. Tolimir, I would like to ask you if you can hear the proceedings in a language you understand, that means if you receive proper translation through your earphones. Thank you. Please, Mr. Tolimir, be reminded that you should indicate to the Chamber immediately if there are any problems in this respect during the hearings at any time. Now I would like to ask for appearances, first for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. My name is Peter McCloskey. Good afternoon, General Tolimir, Mr. Gajic. With me today are the lawyers that will be trying the case with me, and starting from behind me this is Mr. Nelson Thayer, and then Mr. Kweku Vanderpuye, and Mr. Rupert Elderkin. And very importantly, our case manager, Janet Stewart. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And now the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Zdravko Tolimir, that's me, and this is my legal assistant, Aleksandar Gajic. May all the participants in this conference -- may God help all those who are participants in the proceedings and those who will be following the proceedings. May God bless you all and grant you wisdom, and may kind angels follow us in these proceedings through to the end. May all of us here proceed in accordance with our conscience, truth, and justice. May all of us be saved. I love Christ and prefer to live in Christ than I do -- I prefer to live in Christ than I do in my own body. I hope that we will open these proceedings in accordance with the will of God and that it will be useful for our souls and kind to God, and I hope that all of us shall preserve our faith in Jesus Christ and preserve the purity of our lives. May I drink from this chalice in accordance with the will of God. Thank you, may God bless you all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir. I would like to refer to the Chamber's decision of the 22nd of February, this year, by which the Chamber ordered that Mr. Aleksandar Gajic, as the legal advisor of the accused may, be present in the courtroom during the Pre-Trial Conference and the subsequent court proceedings. I would like to note that the last Status Conference in this case was held on the 16th of December, 2009. Two days later, on the 18th of December, last year, the President of this Tribunal issued an order assigning Judges to a case before the Tribunal which defined the composition of the current Bench. With me are Judge Antoine Kesia-Mbe Mindua seated to my right and Judge Prisca Matimba Nyambe seated to my left. No longer with us is Judge Kimberly Prost who was -- who, as a pre-trial Judge for over two and a half years, prepared the case for trial. On behalf of the whole Chamber, I would like to thank her for her effective and fruitful work. We have assembled today in order to prepare the trial in this case which will commence tomorrow in the afternoon with the opening statement of the Prosecution. The purpose of today's hearing is to allow us to deal with a number of matters pursuant to Rule 73 bis of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence. As it currently stands, the Chamber has no reason to call upon the Prosecution to shorten the estimated length of the examination-in-chief of any witness pursuant to Rules 73 bis paragraph (B) of the Rules. However, the Chamber may raise this issue at a later stage of the proceedings if it deems it appropriate to do so. Now I would like to turn to Rule 73 bis, paragraph (C) of the Rules. This concerns the total number of witnesses the Prosecution may call and the time available for the Prosecution for presenting evidence. I note that the Prosecution's motion pursuant to Rule 92 bis filed on the 13th of February last year is still pending. The Chamber will issue a decision in due course, but for today I would like to ask the Prosecution if there are any submissions in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber notes that it didn't invite the Prosecution pursuant to Rule 73 bis paragraph (D) to reduce the number of counts or to fix the number of crime sites or indictments. Neither did the Chamber pursuant to 73 bis paragraph (E) direct the Prosecutor to select the counts in the indictment on which to proceed. Taking into account its discretion in this respect, the Chamber has no reason to deal with this matter. Now I turn to the motions currently pending before this Chamber. First, the Prosecution's 92 bis motion filed on the 13th of February, 2009. As I already have indicated, the Chamber will issue its decision in due course. Then the Prosecution's supplementary notice of disclosure of expert witness reports filed confidentially on the 26th of November last year. The Prosecution's motion to amend the witness list and exhibit lists and for continuance of protective measures filed confidentially on the 15th of December, 2009. Then the Prosecution's motion to amend the witness list and for disclosure of an expert report filed on the 8th of January, 2010. The Prosecution's motion to amend the witness list and for disclosure of an expert report filed on the 26th of January, 2010. The accused's request for the Chamber to order the Prosecution to act in accordance with the -- its obligations proceeding from the Chamber's decision of the 25th of November, 2009, submitted on the 8th of February, 2010. Further, the Prosecution's motion to amend the witness list, admission of evidence pursuant to Rule 92 ter, and protective measures, filed on the 11th of February, 2010. The accused's information and request for the Trial Chamber submitted on the 12th of February, 2010. Finally, still pending is the Prosecution's motion requesting permanent counsel for the accused, for which the Chamber will now issue an oral decision as follows. The Chamber is seized of the Prosecution's motion requesting appointment of permanent counsel for accused -- for the accused, Tolimir, filed on the 29th of April, 2008, and two responses from the accused filed in English on the 19th of May and the 2nd of June, 2008. Considering that the reasons stated in the motion for imposing counsel do not appear to the Chamber to be pertinent at this time, the motion is hereby dismissed without prejudice. However, in the interests of justice, the Chamber finds it appropriate to take this opportunity to remind you, Mr. Tolimir, that the new phase of the proceedings that we are about to enter, the trial phase, will likely about very demanding on you and your legal team. As a self-represented accused, your role will be very different than that of a represented accused before this Chamber. While you will have access to your legal team during the proceedings as well as the possibility of administrative support from the Registry's pro se liaison office, the practicalities of trial will likely limit your ability to consult extensively with either during the hearings. As a self-represented accused, you will be held on the same standards as any counsel practicing before this Tribunal. This means that you must be prepared to address issued as they arise, whether in the context of cross-examination, objections from the opposing party, or questions from the Bench. These proceedings will demand your thorough preparation, full attention, and the most efficient use of all of our time and resources. Furthermore, if at any time you feel as though you are unable to adequately conduct your own defence, you may engage counsel. Lastly, I wish to remind you that pursuant to Rule 45 ter, the Trial Chamber may, if it decides that it is in the interests of justice, instruct the Registrar to assign counsel to represent your interests. The Chamber therefore will closely monitor your conduct in this trial and any impact it may have on the progress of this trial. Mr. Tolimir, do you wish to address the Chamber in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. First of all, I should like to thank you for allowing my legal advisor, Aleksandar Gajic, to participate -- to attend all the sessions, including this conference, and I thank you as the Chamber for your decision. I would like to raise the following request. The Pre-Trial Chamber should allow my legal advisor, Aleksandar Gajic, to take part on my request in the presentation of legal submissions. I should like him to deal with the legal matters in this case, and I seek your leave for this. I should also like him to take part in any other courses of action, of which you will be notified well in advance at my request. Perhaps I should like him to be involved in the examination of witnesses, just as it was granted to Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Djordjevic. If I get your leave for this, I would advance you of -- I would notify you of this well in advance. So I'm merely seeking what has been granted to other accused. I have taken notice of what you have just told me. My legal advisor and I are consulting each other all the time. We are working together, and neither of us want to make any mistakes. He would like to provide me with any advice that I may need, just as provided for in Article 21, para 4 of the Statute of the ICTY. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. Would the Prosecution have a word?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The Prosecution did not -- do not object to Mr. Gajic taking a role in legal matters and legal submissions, and at this stage the rest of the request is fairly broad regarding questioning of witnesses and other items. I don't immediately have any problem with that, but I think it would be a good idea if that was put on paper and the citations that he's referring to of other cases should be noted to us all. But I would leave that into the -- as it is your discretion regarding the rest of it, I would prefer to see it and see the citations about asking questions and things. But as for legal submissions, that would be helpful, no problem whatsoever. The other issues regarding questioning witnesses, I would like a little more time to reflect on. That's the first I've heard of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the position of the Chamber at the moment is I think quite clear, and you can read it in our written decision, that Mr. Gajic is allowed to be present in the courtroom but has no right to address anything to the Chamber. You must be aware of the fact that you are -- have made the decision to be representing yourself. That means you have the full responsibility and the task of a Defence counsel. If you want to have another way of proceeding, then please do it in writing so that the Prosecution and the Chamber is fully aware of your wish and we can then make a further decision on this topic. Thank you very much. Now the Chamber would like to put some questions to the parties in relation to the commencement of trial tomorrow, in particular to the opening statements. First, does the Prosecution have an updated estimated length of its opening statement, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Mr. Thayer will be giving the opening statement, and as we have been getting ready and he's been getting ready he has noted that it -- going into Monday would be the best possible option for him, which you have set aside in any event. And we have been told by Mr. Gajic that General Tolimir does not wish to make an opening statement, so there should be time. But I would -- any further questions, Mr. Thayer is ready to respond to in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think for the moment it is enough. We have now your indication and we will take that into account. Mr. Tolimir, pursuant to Rule 84 of our Rules, in your capacity as Defence counsel you may elect to make your opening statement after the Prosecution's opening statement, tomorrow and Monday, or you may wait until the beginning of the Defence case. Furthermore, pursuant to Rule 84 bis, in your capacity as the accused, and not as Defence or a witness, you may, under the control of the Chamber, make a statement after the Prosecution's opening statement, for which you will be neither compelled to make a solemn declaration nor examined about the content of the statement, and the Chamber shall decide on the probative value, if any, to be attached to the statement. Before you answer regarding your intentions in either one of these respects, I will take the opportunity to say the following. The Chamber is seized of the Prosecution's motion for an instruction regarding the admissibility of submission and statements of the accused filed in English yesterday -- the 23rd of February. The motion asks the Chamber to issue an instruction to you regarding your rights to remain silent and the possible consequences should you choose to waive this right. I understand that you have received the translation for this submission, and I would like to ask you if you are in a position to respond orally at this time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I am in a position to respond orally to these questions that you have raised. As for the latter question, my legal advisor and I have read the motion of the Prosecution, and I can tell you that I will not make an opening statement until I start my case in accordance with the Rules. I will likewise not sign the statement in accordance with my rights. I also wish to let you know that I am fully apprised of my rights, either from the side of my legal advisor or by having read the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Now, the Prosecution's instruction on submissions is not quite appropriate. It states that you may take into account the submissions I make and the submissions my legal advisor makes. I think that you should take them into account, that it would be proper for you, for the Trial Chamber, to take into account any submissions I may make and consider them. I don't think I should give any particular response to the motion by the OTP, since my legal advisor and I have discussed the motion and have taken up this position. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. Nevertheless, in any case the Chamber would like to give you some guidance in this respect, taking into account what you just stated. You have the right to remain silent during the whole trial. You are not obliged to give evidence, to question witnesses, or to make submissions. You may, however, give evidence on your own behalf at the appropriate time, in which case you will be subject to cross-examination. Other than when giving evidence, you are not obliged to answer any questions about the facts of the case, but you should be aware that if you do make statements about the facts during submissions to the Court, such statements may be part of the material considered by the Trial Chamber in reaching its decision on the case. I would like to ask you again: Do you intend to make an opening statement pursuant to Rule 84 or a statement pursuant to Rule 84 bis of the Rules following the Prosecution's opening statement; and if so, do you have an estimate of the length?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My advisor and I have, in deciding about our case, decided that there is no need for us to make an opening statement during the Prosecution case; rather, we shall do this at the stage when the Defence will be presenting their case. Secondly, my legal advisor and I have also decided that we should not be making a statement in accordance with Rule 84 bis and that at this stage we do not wish to make any statements. I hope that I have answered your questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That is clear now. The next issue is the question of agreed facts. At the Status Conference on the 22nd of October, 2009, the Prosecution indicated that it would be in a better position to discuss the subject of agreed facts once the accused's pre-trial brief was translated into English. The English translation was filed on the 28th of October, 2009. Are there any updates from the parties with regards to agreed facts? Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. General Tolimir prefers that all our communications with him go through Mr. Gajic. I have spoken to Mr. Gajic about this topic, and we have been unable to come to even the simplest agreement on the simplest of facts I think is the unfortunate clearest way to say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, do you want to add something? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my learned friend, Mr. McCloskey, for correctly representing the situation. Mr. Gajic has been authorised by me to discuss these matters with the Prosecution. In the submissions filed before the Pre-Trial Chamber, he clearly presented the position of the Defence and clear conclusions can be drawn from there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then we can turn to the next issue, this is the disclosure of materials pursuant to Rule 66 and 68. During the last Status Conference, issues of disclosures from the cases Popovic, Krstic, Blagojevic, and Jokic were raised by the accused. Judge Prost indicated that the disclosures were being processed by the Registry and should be completed soon. The Chamber received an updated from the Registry, with the exception of those materials identified by the Registry as possibly containing personal information, all materials from the cases Popovic, Krstic, Blagojevic and Jokic have been disclosed to the accused. For those materials identified by the Registry as possibly containing personal information, the materials were provided to the counsels for each of the accused in those cases to review. I understand that the disclosure from the Popovic case is complete and the Registry is currently awaiting responses from the counsels for Krstic, Blagojevic, and Jokic, which I expected very soon. Are there any updates from the parties regarding disclosure? Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I don't have any updates. I can just tell you that the disclosure is ongoing and I would like to thank the Registry for having enabled us to get access of all the necessary materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has met its obligations under this rule. It's a continuing process, as you know. In fact, you may have seen in the public there are ongoing searches in Serbia of places, and we have been obtaining material almost on a regular basis for the last several years that we endeavour to review and provide to the accused in an indexed form so that the documents can be seen without having to go through everything at first. And so that is what we will continue to endeavour to do. There are more materials coming in. We will get that to them in electronic format as soon as possible. These are many of the reasons you see these ongoing and what is relatively normal requests for new exhibits and such. But we are pretty much caught up with all the material from the past Srebrenica trials and of course are always open for General Tolimir, if he has any specific requests that he wants us to search for exculpatory material regarding Rule 68, that's certainly not his obligation to do that, but that does assist us if there's something in particular he's looking for. Counsel for various accused have asked us to do that in the past and that is something we are, of course, most willing to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. McCloskey. Furthermore, the Chamber reminds the Prosecution pursuant to Rule 66 to disclose to the accused in a language he understands statements of all witnesses whom the Prosecutor intends to call to testify at trial and copies of all transcripts and written statements taken in accordance with Rule 92 bis, ter, and quater. Furthermore, the Chamber reminds the Prosecution pursuant to Rule 68 it must disclose to the Defence in a timely manner any material the Prosecutor knows could suggest the innocence or mitigate the guilt of the accused or affect the credibility of the Prosecution evidence. This remains of course an ongoing obligation. The next topic would be the trial management. A trial management meeting, TMM, will be held on the 5th of March. Parties are invited to take part. Mr. Tolimir, you have indicated that you will not attend this meeting. Because you will not be present, there will be no B/C/S interpretation of the meeting. The transcript and audio/visual record will be in English, copies of which you may of course request. Furthermore, yesterday the Chamber issued an order concerning guide-lines on the presentation of evidence and conduct of parties during trial. The Chamber has taken the necessary steps to provide you, Mr. Tolimir, with a B/C/S translation as soon as possible. Perhaps you have received it during today. This order relates in particular to the following: Co-operation between the parties; efficient use of time; outlined procedure for tendering, numbering, and admission of exhibits; Rule 92 ter procedure; notice of witnesses, witness schedules, and documents for examine and cross; e-court uploading, and I should add procedural issues should be dealt with as much as possible in writing. I refer the parties to this order and ask that it about kept in mind as the trial progresses. Now a word about e-court. Parties are reminded that this is an e-court trial and hard copies should be avoided as much as possible. However, if the parties feel that it is absolutely necessary to provide the Chamber or a witness with a hard copy, they may do so. Are there any updates by the parties regarding e-court matters? Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm informed that all the key material is in e-court for the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All the original materials. These additional motions that are outstanding have, of course, not been uploaded as yet, but they of course will be in due course if the rulings go that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, do you want to comment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no comment and I would like to thank everybody who provided me with everything that I need for my defence well in time. I have all the confidence in my legal advisor, who is going to attend the meeting that you have just mentioned. On Monday mornings I can't attend any activities because I have to attend a church service. This is not possible on Sunday because on Sunday our priest cannot come to the Detention Unit. Therefore, we attend a service on Mondays and Croats attend service on Fridays. Therefore, I would kindly ask you if at all possible not to have anything scheduled on Monday mornings, but rather on Monday afternoon. I can see that for the month of March only one session was scheduled on Monday morning, on the 29th of March. I would kindly ask you if at all possible to change that to another day or to Monday afternoon. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Taking into account the problems of scheduling and three courtrooms, I can't promise that to you, but we will take that into consideration. Thank you. Now, the Chamber would like to give some information on scheduling of hearings. For at least the first two months of the trial we will only sit two days a week because of occupation of courtrooms, I just mentioned that, and the engagement of two Judges of this Bench in other ongoing cases. We will re-visit the schedule as necessary as the trial progresses. The next topic relates to protective measures. The Chamber considers that first and foremost it is of greatest importance to protect confidential information. Parties are reminded to apply for protective measures as early as possible. Does Mr. McCloskey or the Prosecution foresee requests for protective measures for any of the witnesses scheduled for the coming weeks?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We will begin with some of the survivor witnesses, some of whom have requested protective measures in the past. And as I mentioned to Mr. Gajic, it's from our 65 ter witness list if there is a PW number next to the witness's name, that's an indication they had protective measures in the last trial, which should hold over for this trial. The -- and so as we confirm that with the witnesses and we have been in touch with the first few witnesses and are hearing "yes" in some cases and "no" in others, we will get that out immediately to the Trial Chamber and to the parties of course. And, for example, the witness that we would like to call first asked for facial distortion last time, and we'll have to see how he is now. It tends to change, as I'm sure you're, on their experience after or during the last Trial Chamber or their experience in Bosnia even after all these years. But if we -- as we get that information, we will let you know. Some witnesses choose to go open now, as before they didn't. So we will get that out as we know it. We are, of course, in contact with those first few witnesses, and we expect to be able to get the word out soon. We are -- we are in the unfortunate situation of one of our first witnesses was a shared Karadzic witness, and we're waiting for the Karadzic decision in order to determine whether that witness will be able to be first or not. So -- and I've discussed this with Mr. Gajic and -- but we'll get that out as soon as we can and we'll always about cognisant of it. But if you see that PW number next to a witness, that's an indication that they are -- that they did have protective measures and may be asking -- may very well likely be asking for it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. The Chamber would appreciate to receive these requests as soon as possible, and for the procedure to give pseudonyms, you should liaise with the Registry. The Registry is, of course, the best place to deal with this matter. Thank you very much. I think we have dealt with the most important and all the necessary topics. I would like to ask parties if there are any other items to be raised by the parties now in the Pre-Trial Conference. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just one simple issue regarding a potential sight visit, just to -- if I would ask the Court to, as I'm sure you must have in mind, whether that's something you want to do. I -- personally I think it's advisable but not essential, and I've spoken to Mr. Gajic on that point, but it does take a lot of logistical planning and all. And we've found that the best time to go to Bosnia is May or June when it looks like it did -- roughly looks like it did in the -- during the events but is not so hot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Chamber will consider that matter at a later stage. Mr. Tolimir, do you want to raise any issue?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to ask you once again to bear in mind that on the 29th of March is the last service on the eve of Easter and the resurrection of Christ. That's why I kindly requested you to schedule that in the afternoon. I want to attend the service on that day, and I ask for your indulgence and understanding. As you know, we are allowed to attend religious services in the detention but not on Sunday but rather on Monday and the rest on Friday. And I'm sure that somebody will accommodate your request and swap slots with you. The second thing I would like to raise is to issue a decision as soon as possible about the Prosecution's request pursuant to Rule 92 bis, a matter that Mr. McCloskey has just commented upon. We as Defence want to have as many elements to devise our strategy, to be able to call our witnesses, and to schedule their sequence. I would kindly ask you to issue that decision as soon as possible. I would also like to inform you that the Defence is having a very hard time, because we cannot complete our Defence due to some decisions on the part of the Registry when it comes to financing. The 150 hours that are paid to me are not enough to organise my Defence. Please bear that in mind because I need to be able to have the equality of arms in these proceedings that have been accorded to all the other accused and that has been accorded to the OTP. I believe that we will have an opportunity to discuss the situation in the Detention Unit, but for the time being I would like to thank you for your kind attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir. Three points you have raised. The first is the scheduling on the 29th of March. As you know, we are in the hands of those people in the administration who make the scheduling, but we will consider your request immediately after this Pre-Trial Conference, and I understand -- we understand your situation. The second, as I indicated already to you, that the decision on the motion of the Prosecution related to 92 bis is -- will be decided in due course. And the third matter, you know the Registry is responsible for that and will deal with this, I think as well, in due course. Thank you very much. We adjourn now and we'll resume tomorrow in the afternoon at 2.15 in this courtroom for the opening statement of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.01 p.m.
